title: Grief can change the shape of your heart 💔
subject: heart
description:
Has this happened to someone you know? 👇

Takotsubo syndrome, or broken heart syndrome, was first described in Japan in 1990. A surge of adrenaline after a shock makes the left ventricle balloon into the shape of an octopus trap. It mimics a heart attack, but the arteries are clear. This video is not medical advice.

Sources: Sian E. Harding, BBC Science Focus, "Broken Heart Syndrome: How scientists unravelled the cardiac mystery" (2022)
tags: can you die of a broken heart

scenes.text: A shock can bend your heart into a new shape.
Doctors in Japan described it in 1990. The tip of the left ventricle stalls and balloons out.
On the scan it looked like a Takotsubo, a Japanese pot for trapping octopus.
The trigger is a surge of adrenaline, often after a loved one dies.
It mimics a heart attack, yet the arteries are clear. Up to 90 percent of patients are women.
Most recover completely, sometimes within days, and the heart regains its shape.
